method: Static reverse engineering; no sample or package code executed. atomscan --no-update --mode=slow --follow=none --format=json and cleave facts on each supplied path; rizin disassembly, UPX decompression, binwalk and source review.

analysis.identity: QueenKarton_12 banking trojan, consistent with Berbew/Padodor/Qukart/Hangup aliases
evidence: 0x406075 builds a fake Authorization Failed window with Visa/MasterCard choices, card number, CVV2 and ATM PIN edit controls; 0x406449 supplies the deceptive transaction/PIN explanation.

0x406c29 copies the running image into the system directory, calls the COM registration routine at 0x403f68, launches the copy and exits. The registration routine writes ShellServiceObjectDelayLoad and CLSID InProcServer32 entries.
0x406f37 resolves RegisterServiceProcess, then calls it with the current PID and registration=1, hiding the task on Windows 9x.

Embedded DLL at file offset 0x7e84: DllMain reaches an arithmetic-junked launcher at VA 0x10001349; checks MMM_HT mutex, constructs a system-directory path and calls WinExec. This proves no search-order hijack.
binwalk also identifies an appended copy of the PE at 0x15000. Card prompts following the embedded DLL mapped sections belong to parent-file data and must not be labeled as DLL phishing.
changes: Move neutral card prompts, WinExec API co-occurrence, service API name, registry path and UI symbol to capability homes. Move two Berbew identity strings to family identity.

Require the deceptive PIN explanation for phishing and malicious shell-service autoload; relocate autoload out of COM hijacking. Retire redundant size/import-only launcher conclusions while preserving the malware-family consumer conjunction.
Require mapped-section prompt evidence, preventing inheritance from carved overlay bytes. Tighten incidental XOR cmd and prose computer matches.

analysis.identity: talahon-agent 2.0.4, Talon in-container SOC analyst runtime
evidence: Cargo metadata declares the Talon workspace and disables a build script. The archive contains Rust runtime, supervisor, sessions, tool integration and tests, with no hidden executable payload.

Supervisor starts configured MCP servers under distinct non-root users with scrubbed environments, verifies Unix-socket peers, and drops agent UID/GID. Sessions use private file/directory modes. These implement the documented privilege separation.
Agent runs a configured vLLM/tool loop and emits local structured triage reports. Script execution is an explicit task feature with cancellation and timeout handling.
src/supervise.rs, agent.rs, run.rs, script.rs and mcp.rs exactly match public VCS commit 20472b20dd4075d0a68fff1e48d761faf7609aaf.
changes: Match --agent as a complete Rust literal, so --agent-user is not hidden-agent execution. Ignore negated secret-read statements. Move the ordinary /report path from C2 to URL-path references.

analysis.identity: Eupdate Helper 4.0.1.0 by yztcsn, UPX-packed ESET update mirror
evidence: UPX decompression yields a 138478-byte MinGW executable. The relay requests vendor ESET manifests using a rotating list of trial accounts, maps update.ver paths and relays content.

0x4146c7 tests a .signed suffix and returns HTTP 404 at 0x41472f. This is an unsupported-resource response, not proof that antivirus definition updates are withheld or signature verification is patched.
0x417c40 strips SERVERS/LINKS/HOSTS routing sections. There is no demonstrated malicious module substitution, credential theft, or disabled security product.
0x412964 fetches update metadata; MessageBoxW at 0x412c6e gates replacement on user acceptance, with a separate declined branch at 0x412f54.

0x4127e4 appends random bytes to the image; a standby process relaunches it. Keep this unusual hash rotation suspicious. Run registration and ordinary updating alone do not establish malicious persistence.

Port-owner termination and relaxed WinHTTP certificate checks remain visible as capabilities. The supplied sandbox score and public AV labels were considered but do not replace proof of hostile behavior.
changes: Retire unsupported hostile AV-tampering and hash-rotating-persistence composites. Keep relay, networking, TLS, process, autostart and update observations, plus one suspicious hash-rotation finding. No application-name allowlist added.

limitations: The supplied VirusTotal and Triage pages could not be retrieved by the web tool. Decisions rest on the supplied bytes and inspected code, not a claimed independent sandbox run.
No supplied finding was attributed to a fetched hostile dependency; dependency-specific suppression or PURL rescans were therefore unnecessary.
